title: Minimum Number of Operations to Have Distinct Elements
summary: Given an integer array, repeatedly remove the first three elements in each operation.
statement: Given an integer array, repeatedly remove the first three elements in each operation. If fewer than three elements remain, remove all. Continue until no duplicates are left. Return the count of operations performed.
constraints: nums contains between one and 100,000 positive integers.
One operation removes the first three elements, or all remaining elements when fewer than three remain.
Stop as soon as all remaining elements are distinct.
hints: After k operations, exactly the suffix beginning at index 3k remains.
Scan backward while maintaining the distinct suffix seen so far.
At the first repeated value at index i, remove through the block containing i: floor(i/3)+1 operations.
Every later suffix is distinct by the scan, while retaining index i preserves its duplicate.
editorial: Every later suffix is distinct by the scan, while retaining index i preserves its duplicate.

tests.explanation: Removing the first three leaves [6,5,8], whose values are distinct, so one operation suffices.
The original array is already distinct, so no operation is needed.
